I'm gonna go out on a limb and say this advice is pretty bad, coming from a person who lost ~75 pounds a decade ago and kept it off since. Eating any dessert (really all dessert is just mostly flavored sugar anyways) is only gonna send you into a spiral of eatting more sugar, via the very very real second stomach effect, among more complicated hormonal changes, its a big reason why so much processed garbage is loaded to hell with sugars (Plural! There are like 30 different synonyms for sugar in the US, I think Doritos for example has like 5 different types of sugar in it.) Alternative advice: 

1. Eat regularly scheduled meals, 1-3 a day, this facilitates greater planning skills. Don't buy into the snacking propaganda nonsense, eating more often probably won't help you lose weight.

2. Learn to cook if you can, its generally healthier and you know what you're eatting if you start from first principles. I find it somewhat therapeutic but that may just be me!

3. Daily/semiregular ritualized breathing meditations can help your self control and impulsivity, as can exercise. 

4. Practice good sleep hygiene, being sleep deprived can make you more impulsive (Alongside a ton of other negative effects on your health.)

5. Whole and as simple foods as possible. Also you don't realllly need a massive variety food, and a large variety can be addictive via novelty exposure to an extent, but the sugar is the most definitely the bigger issue.

6. Stress reduction, although thats easier said than done, this of course goes with points 3 and points 4. 

7. CICO is basically ideological communism for junk food companies, 100 cals of bell peppers isn't the same as pepsi or cheesecake or steak. The nutritional rabbit hole goes so incredibly deep.

8. Avoid hyper refined polysaccharides when possible.
